newsitem.title: CHINA: Gore arrives in China on fence-mending visit.
newsitem.headline: Gore arrives in China on fence-mending visit.

text.p: U.S. Vice President Al Gore arrived in Beijing on Monday in a bid to heal strained Sino-U.S. ties and pave the way for an exchange of presidential visits.
Gore told reporters shortly before he left Tokyo for Beijing that he would raise human rights issues with Chinese leaders but had no plans for specific meetings with human rights activists.
Sino-U.S. relations had been badly strained by disputes ranging from human rights to trade and Taiwan, but Washington and Beijing have been working hard to improve ties.
Gore is the most senior U.S. official to travel to China since then-President George Bush visited Beijing in early 1989.
The vice president's trip has already been marred by a controversy over U.S. accusations that China may have made illegal contributions to the Democratic Party.

The official People's Daily said on Monday that the Chinese government had not made any payments to the Democratic Party and that an improvement in Sino-U.S. ties was due to efforts by the two governments and their people.
